newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka president set to reshuffle cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka president set to reshuffle cabinet.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga was preparing on Monday to reshuffle her 23-member cabinet for the first time since her People's Alliance government took power in 1994, officials said.
They said Kumaratunga was likely to promote some junior ministers and change the portfolios of a few cabinet members in an attempt to rationalise duties.
Newspaper reports said more than six ministries were to change hands and at least three new ministers were to be appointed.
No official confirmation of the details was available.

Speculation has been rife in recent weeks about the fate of Srimani Athulathmudali, Minister of Transport, Environment, and Women's Affairs. Newspaper reports said she would either be removed or her portfolios pruned because of policy differences between her and the government.
Athulathmudali heads the Democratic United National Front, a member of the ruling seven-party coalition.
Analysts said Labour Minister Mahinda Rajapakse might be given another portfolio after he was criticised by the business lobby of being too pro-labour.

Media, Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Dharmasiri Senanayake might also have at least one of his portfolios pruned. The government recently faced embarrassment over its proposed Broadcast Bill, designed to curb the private radio and television stations by making it necessary for them to renew their licences each year.
The bill was shot down by the Supreme Court last month after it was challenged by various media organisations as well as the main opposition United National Party.
